description: Saved pagination observations 21 and 37 from audit d8ae8860; GET source only, no model request required.

findings.title: GET messages endpoint fetches all messages for a match with no pagination limit
findings.fix_hint: Add a `.limit(200)` (or similar) to the initial query and document that clients should use `?after=` for incremental loading. Alternatively, always require the client to paginate using cursor-based pagination.
findings.explanation: The GET handler for messages fetches all messages for a match in a single query with no LIMIT. For active matches with many messages over time, this query will return an unbounded number of rows, increasing database read costs and response payload size. The `?after=` parameter provides incremental loading but only when the client passes it; the initial load (no `after` parameter) always fetches everything.

claim_evidence.observation: The query at lines 55-59 selects all columns from messages for a match_id with no `.limit()`. The `afterTs` branch at line 61 adds a `.gt()` filter but only when the client provides the parameter.
